kaylaTokenAdherence.enforcedBy: npm run lint:tokens (see package.json). Every rule here is an error, not a warning.
whyNotUnderRules: oxlint 1.83.0 does not implement `no-restricted-syntax` — it rejects the config outright with
"Rule 'no-restricted-syntax' not found in plugin 'eslint'". The rule set it does ship is
no-restricted-imports / -globals / -exports / -properties, none of which can match a literal's
value. So the three hard-coded-value rules live here as data and are enforced by the scanner half
of `npm run lint:tokens`, which uses these exact patterns and messages.
When oxlint ships no-restricted-syntax, move these three into `rules` as
["error", {selector, message}, ...] and drop the scanner. Nothing else has to change.
droppedFromSource: no-restricted-imports — it forbids reaching past a design_system/index.js barrel that does not
exist in this repo. kayla-frontend consumes the design system as GENERATED TOKENS
(src/styles/tokens.css), not as a JavaScript package, so the rule could never fire and would
read as protection we do not have.
react/forbid-elements — shipped with an empty `forbid` list; a rule that forbids nothing.
The ~100 component prop-contract selectors — they name design-system components (Button, Icon,
EmployeeCard, ...) that this repo does not yet contain. They belong in the phase that ports them,
where they can be error-level against real usage.

rules.message: Raw hex color — use a design-system color token via var().
Raw px value — use a design-system spacing token via var().
Font not provided by the design system. Available: Plus Jakarta Sans, Manrope, Inter — or a --font-* token via var().

adaptedFromSource: non-ds-font-family differs from the upstream selector in two ways, both load-bearing:
1. It allows `var(--font-...)`. Upstream only allowed the three family names spelled out, which would
have failed the one correct way to set a family here: `font-family: var(--font-core)` (R5 — the
2. The negative lookahead now starts with \s*. Upstream reads `\s*(?!['\"]?(?:Plus Jakarta Sans|...))`,
and because \s* backtracks to zero width the lookahead is evaluated ON the space after the colon —
so `font-family: Inter` matches the rule that is supposed to permit Inter. Upstream flags every
declaration written with a space after the colon, including the compliant ones.
